title: 1967 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Given the two hypotheses: I Some Mems are not Ens and II No Ens are Vees. If “some” means “at least one,” we can conclude that:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
Neither \((A)\) nor \((B)\) nor \((C)\) nor
\((D)\) is deducible from the given statements

solutions.text:
The hypotheses say only that some element of \(M\) lies outside \(N,\) and that \(N\cap V=\varnothing.\) A model with \(M=V\) makes (A), (B), and (C) false while satisfying the hypotheses. A model with \(M\cap V=\varnothing\) makes (D) false. Hence none of choices (A) through (D) is forced.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Translate the three kinds of objects into sets \(M,N,V\)
Test both \(M=V\) and \(M\cap V=\varnothing\) while keeping the two hypotheses true
